scenes.heading: Building a repeatable watchlist and screening process

sents.d: Building a repeatable watchlist and screening process
Scanning the entire market for ideas every day is a good way to end up chasing noise.

A watchlist — a small, consistently reviewed set of instruments you actually understand — beats scanning the whole market daily for 'what's moving,' which tends to pull you into unfamiliar setups and impulsive decisions.

scenes.heading: Screen the same way every time

sents.d: A simple, repeatable screening process (a handful of criteria you check the same way every time) removes a lot of the emotional decision-making that leads to inconsistent results, since you're applying the same standard regardless of how a day is going.
Reviewing your watchlist periodically — dropping instruments that no longer fit your criteria, adding new ones deliberately — keeps it useful instead of becoming a stale list you stop actually using.

take: Keep a focused watchlist and a fixed screening checklist.
